Nate Sheets

Republican candidate for Commissioner of Agriculture, Texas

Agriculture entrepreneur (per campaign site)

Nate Sheets is the Republican nominee for Texas Commissioner of Agriculture. His campaign describes him as a fifth-generation Texan, a Navy veteran and an agriculture entrepreneur. He advanced to the November 3, 2026 general election by defeating incumbent Sid Miller in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary.

Where Sheets stands

Support for agricultural producers
Says he will be a strong partner to Texas producers, helping them "grow better food and grow food better," and will advocate for people who produce food.
Food quality and children's health
Proposes working with the Legislature, farmers and producers to make sure children eat the cleanest food possible.
Federal coordination and food supply protection
Says the Texas Department of Agriculture should work closely with the Trump administration to protect farmers, producers and the nation's food supply.
Immigration and border security
Says he will support the Trump administration's efforts to secure the border and stop illegal immigration into Texas.
Abortion
Describes himself as pro-life and says he would use the office to promote healthy babies, adoption opportunities and economic stability for families.
Agency reform
Says he is running to change practices at the Texas Department of Agriculture. He has publicly criticized incumbent Sid Miller's management of the department.
Rural economy
During his "Texans Should Feed Texans" rural bus tour, he said he wants to remove economic barriers in agriculture.
